Dimensionality Reduction:
Dimensionality Reduction is the process of reducing the
number of variables (features) in a dataset while retaining
the most important information. It is crucial for simplifying
models, improving performance and visualizing Data.
Two Categories exist:
1 Linear Methods like PCA and LDA
2 Non-linear methods like LLE and Isomap
1 Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA): LDA is a supervised
Learning technique that finds a projection of Data onto
a lower-dimensional space to maximum class
separability. Unlike PCA, which focuses on variance. LDA
uses labels to improve predictive performance.
-> It is particularly useful when the Dataset has
class labels and the goal is to maximize class
seperability by projecting the Data onto a lower-
dimensional space.
Key objectives of LDA:
1 Maximize seperation Between classes: LDA projects data
in a way that maximizes the distance Between the
means of different classes.
2 Maximize variance within classes: It also maximizes
scatter or variance within Each class.
